findings.F1: Over the next 24 hours a coin reverses its own 24-hour return, and the reversal grows with the size of that return. Measured on the 24-bar grid, the reversal rises from -4.9 bp in the smallest |24h return| quintile to +13.4 bp in the fourth and +64.3 bp in the largest (t 5.1, 2585 cases). Read as a slope, it is +52.6 bp per usual 24h move of |24h return| (t 8.9, 12926 cases).
findings.F2: In the largest |24h return| quintile the reversal holds across the data. It is positive in every coin, from +50.9 bp in ETH to +86.5 bp in ZEC (t 1.5 to 3.2, about 435 cases each), and in 79 % of the 24 windows. Its strength is 0.13 of the coin's usual 24h move, well above the 0.05 typical of real ideas. Its total move of +63.6 bp is 3.3 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F3: The reversal is lopsided by side. After the largest 24h falls the next 24h excess return is +96.9 bp (t 5.1, 1240 cases), against +34.2 bp of reversal after the largest 24h rises (t 2.1, 1345 cases).
findings.F4: The 24h reversal is concentrated where 24h volatility is high against its 30-day level. It is +56.3 bp in the top quintile of vol24/vol720 (t 4.7, 2585 cases), against -14.8 to +15.6 bp in the other four (|t| below 1.8).
findings.F5: The 2-hour move also reverses over the next 8 hours, graded by its size: from -1.3 bp in the smallest |2h| quintile to +6.4 bp (t 2.4) in the fourth and +15.7 bp (t 4.1, 10369 cases) in the largest. This total move is below the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F6: The 8h reversal of the 2h move is not tied to funding times. At the 08:00 settlement it is -2.8 bp (t -1.2), while at 04:00, a time with no funding, it is +4.5 bp (t 2.2), next to +12.2 bp at 00:00 (t 6.1) and +7.3 bp at 16:00 (t 3.3; about 17300 cases each). The idea's own measure has a strength of 0.007 and a mean of only +0.02 % per case (t 1.25).
findings.F7: The book lost through its shorts. Short trades averaged -0.41 % before fees against +0.23 % for longs (about 16000 trades each side). The book's daily mean was negative every year from 2022 to 2025 (-8.5 to -11.9 bp, t -2.6 to -3.8), for a Sharpe of -0.83.
findings.F8: The 1-hour excess return has a clock pattern unrelated to settlement. It is high on bars closing at 21:00 and 22:00 UTC (+4.8 bp t 6.0, +3.7 bp t 4.8) and low on bars closing at 14:00 and 03:00 (-4.2 bp t -4.5, -3.4 bp t -4.6). Volume is highest from 15:00 to 17:00 (median 1.47 to 1.52 of the weekly median), not at the settlement hours.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 24-hour return relative to its usual 24-hour move, the more strongly its price moves the opposite way over the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: After an unusually large 24-hour move a trader leans against it for the next day, more heavily the larger the move, and refuses to chase it.
ideas.name: large daily move reverses

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's 24-hour fall relative to its usual 24-hour move, the larger its rise over the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a coin after a sharp one-day fall, sized by the depth of the fall, rather than shorting the weakness.
ideas.name: sharp daily fall rebounds

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour volatility is high against its 30-day volatility, its 24-hour return reverses over the next 24 hours, and the higher that ratio, the larger the reversal.
ideas.consequence: A trader fades the last day's move mostly when the coin has just turned unusually volatile, and more as the volatility burst grows.
ideas.name: volatility burst move reverses

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 2-hour return relative to its usual 2-hour move, the more its price moves the opposite way over the next 8 hours, at any time of day.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans against a sharp 2-hour move for the next 8 hours, sized by its size, without waiting for a funding time.
ideas.name: sharp two-hour move reverses
